claims.text: Selective surface segregation of Al occurs in CoCrFeNiAl high-entropy nanoalloys at high temperature.
Segregated Al forms a continuous protective Al2O3 layer on nanoparticle surfaces and grain boundaries under oxidizing conditions.
The Al2O3 layer stabilizes the nanoalloy structure under oxidizing conditions.
An Al concentration critical for surface segregation and protective-oxide formation exists.
Isoelectronic substitution can produce an Al-lean control with chemistry and microstructure comparable to the Al-containing alloy while removing its ability to form alumina.
High mixing entropy ensures an initially homogeneous single-phase state in the proposed nanoalloy.
At elevated temperature, kinetic factors drive Al migration toward surfaces and grain boundaries.
Al at surfaces and grain boundaries oxidizes preferentially to form adherent alumina.
The alumina layer limits further atomic diffusion.
The alumina layer retards grain-boundary migration.
Limiting diffusion and grain-boundary migration prevents excessive particle coarsening and grain growth.
After oxidation near 800°C for 10–20 hours, Al-containing nanoalloys will exhibit less particle coarsening and grain growth than the Al-lean control.
TEM and EELS will reveal an alumina-rich surface layer only in the Al-bearing nanoalloys.
Comparable nanoalloys that do not form a protective alumina layer will undergo greater grain growth and particle coarsening under the same oxidizing treatment.
The proposed protective mechanism operates under oxidizing conditions around 800°C.
At lower temperatures, Al segregation and oxide formation may be kinetically insufficient to produce the stabilizing effect.
In an inert atmosphere, the stabilizing effect associated with alumina formation may not occur.

contradictions.description: The samples are described as differing only in Al or solely by the presence of Al, but the control is also said to contain an unspecified isoelectronic substitute. Adding a substitute introduces another compositional difference unless its identity and amount are explicitly incorporated into the comparison.
